Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that cardiovascular evaluation may not be strictly necessary before and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas. However, a pretreatment ECG is generally recommended to monitor patients with an unremarkable cardiovascular history and normal heart rate and blood pressure.

During treatment, hypotension may occur due to the potential loss of arterial vasomotor tone after prolonged cardiac arrest. In this case, exogenous pressors may be necessary to maintain vital organ perfusion pressures and improve outcomes.

It is essential to note that the specific patient population, clinical scenario, and current medical guidelines should be considered when determining the necessity of cardiovascular evaluation before and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas.
